> **This is the first run where the engine enforces the answer rather than asking for it, and the
> number is 0% because the enforcement is deterministic.** Three earlier runs, all prompt-only, read 70%,
> 55% and 65% unsupported: the wording changes moved 2 or 3 answers out of 20 and the third made it worse
> in kind, the model decorating its denials ("No chest pain. Just this stubborn cough.") instead of
> writing a bare "No.".
>
> What changed is not a better prompt. The judge now says whether a line asked for information a case
> file would hold (asksAboutFacts), so the engine can tell a question the case cannot answer from small
> talk, and on the first kind it asks the model again and then replaces the answer outright. 103 calls
> against 90 questions means 13 replies were caught and asked again; every one of the 20 ended honest,
> and 9 of them in the patient's own words rather than the fallback.
>
> Read the 0% as "the guard holds", not as "the model learned". The model still asserts something on
> better than half of these questions; what changed is that it no longer reaches the candidate.
